entries.title: Browser Navigation and Continuity
entries.description: Open and follow pages, inspect visual or embedded obstacles, recover stale controls, verify results, and reuse or close completed task pages.

entries.title: Visual CAPTCHA Handling
entries.description: Inspect a visible CAPTCHA with the model’s own vision, interact with current browser controls, and verify the outcome without solver APIs.

entries.title: Read a PDF for evidence
entries.description: Read a PDF's relevant pages, verify table labels and units, and cite the evidence used in the answer.

entries.title: Review a Word document
entries.description: Read Word paragraphs and tables, give located revisions, or save and inspect the edited document requested.

entries.title: Compare document versions
entries.description: Compare two document versions and locate changes to wording, obligations, dates, amounts, or conclusions.

entries.title: Extract actions from documents
entries.description: Extract actions, named owners, deadlines, decisions, and source locations from notes or documents.

entries.title: Inspect spreadsheet data
entries.description: Read workbook sheets and stored cells, distinguish formulas from cached values, and reconcile relevant totals.

entries.title: Clean and reconcile CSV data
entries.description: Parse and clean CSV rows, account for duplicates, and check counts and totals in the saved output.

entries.title: Calculate from tables
entries.description: Calculate from table rows with stated units and denominators, then check the result against the source.

entries.title: Reconcile two lists
entries.description: Match two lists and account for exact, normalized, ambiguous, duplicate, and unmatched records.

entries.title: Job Search
entries.description: Find current openings, verify the exact posting against owner scope, and complete requested applications.

entries.title: Research a public question
entries.description: Research a factual question, read the relevant sources, and link each finding to its supporting evidence.

entries.title: Summarize a web page
entries.description: Read a specified web page and summarize its relevant findings, dates, exceptions, and scope.

entries.title: Compare practical options
entries.description: Compare practical options against the user's requirements and recommend the best supported fit.

entries.title: Write an evidence brief
entries.description: Organize source evidence around a decision and state findings, disagreements, and the next useful action.

entries.title: Draft for a specific audience
entries.description: Write a complete message or short document for its reader, purpose, and requested tone.

entries.title: Edit prose for clarity
entries.description: Make prose easier to follow while preserving facts, intended meaning, and qualifications that matter.

entries.title: Prepare a project handoff
entries.description: Record usable work, unfinished steps, exact artifacts, check results, and the next executable action.

entries.title: Steerability
entries.description: Apply a user's stop or change of direction and preserve the actual results of work already started.

entries.title: Diagnose a software bug
entries.description: Trace a software symptom to the first wrong result, test the cause, and verify a requested repair.

entries.title: Verify a code change
entries.description: Run checks that expose the changed behavior and nearby regressions; report actual outcomes and missing checks.

entries.title: Review a code change
entries.description: Review a patch for concrete behavior defects and report their trigger, effect, source location, and repair direction.

entries.title: Map an unfamiliar code path
entries.description: Trace a repository input through its handlers, saved state, and output using file and symbol references.

entries.title: Draw a concept diagram
entries.description: Create and inspect a labeled static SVG that explains one process, hierarchy, or system relationship.

entries.title: Spot-check web accessibility
entries.description: Check keyboard navigation, visible focus, labels, and reflow on a page or short flow.

entries.title: Tell a story with a chart
entries.description: Calculate the relevant values, create a labeled static chart, and compare it with the source data.

entries.title: Personal Context
aliases: pick up where we left off
entries.description: Use relevant user preferences and prior decisions while keeping the current task's scope and deadline.

entries.title: Intent Inference
entries.description: Resolve references, timing, and scope from the current request and take the next useful step.

entries.title: What Makes Done
entries.description: Check the requested outcome, reassess methods against the full task, and continue missing work or report the actual stop condition.

entries.title: Critical Path
entries.description: Find the unmet dependency that controls delivery and take the most useful available action.

entries.title: Long-Term Judgment
entries.description: Choose effort and complexity according to actual use, expected benefit, delay, and recoverable failure.

entries.title: Verify a Working Slice
entries.description: Follow a representative input through the real workflow and inspect the result where it is used.

entries.title: Expand a Catalog
entries.description: Add distinct catalog entries, verify their references, and check the behavior each choice promises.

entries.title: Anti-Completion Bias
entries.description: Catch a premature final answer and take the next available step while requested work remains.

entries.title: Modular Development
entries.description: Build, fix, or refactor software in small saved changes with observable behavior, focused checks, and visible failure recovery.

entries.title: First Principles Reasoning
entries.description: Rebuild an unfamiliar problem from mechanisms, constraints and evidence. Challenge inherited assumptions, compare designs, select relevant reasoning methods, and test the decisive unknown.

entries.title: Bound the System
entries.description: Define system boundaries, timescales, inputs, outputs, actors, and external conditions before reasoning about capacity, cost, failures, or end-to-end behavior.

entries.title: Decompose from First Principles
entries.description: Rebuild an explanation or solution from components, mechanisms, definitions, observations, and actual constraints; question inherited assumptions without discarding valid empirical knowledge.

entries.title: Track Consequential Assumptions
entries.description: Identify which unverified premises drive a conclusion, distinguish assumptions from observations, and choose checks according to whether they could change the next action.

entries.title: Reconcile Constraints and Feasibility
entries.description: Determine whether requirements can coexist, distinguish hard limits from preferences, and isolate the smallest conflicting set in schedules, budgets, specifications, and resource plans.

entries.title: Check Dimensions and Units
entries.description: Verify equations, conversions, rates, memory estimates, and resource calculations by tracking units, stock-versus-flow meaning, and dimensional consistency.

entries.title: Estimate Scale and Dominant Terms
entries.description: Make Fermi estimates and order-of-magnitude bounds for cost, storage, runtime, demand, or capacity; refine the inputs that dominate the answer.

entries.title: Test Limits and Boundary Cases
entries.description: Challenge formulas, algorithms, and explanations with zero, maximum, symmetric, degenerate, and extreme cases to expose contradictions and establish valid scope.

entries.title: Balance Stocks, Flows, and Residuals
entries.description: Reconcile inventories, task counts, money, data, material, or energy by accounting for opening state, additions, removals, transformations, and closing state.

entries.title: Trace Evidence and Provenance
entries.description: Trace claims to original observations, identify copied reports and shared sources, and preserve dates, versions, scope, and transformations when evaluating evidence.

entries.title: Test Whether Evidence Supports the Claim
entries.description: Check that sources, measurements, and tests support the exact conclusion, including quantifiers, population, version, conditions, and the difference between intermediate and final outcomes.

entries.title: Compare Competing Hypotheses
entries.description: Diagnose ambiguous observations by comparing rival explanations, their predictions, contradicting evidence, and the next observation that can separate them.

entries.title: Draw a Causal Model
entries.description: Represent mechanisms, confounders, mediators, selection effects, and temporal order with a causal graph before interpreting correlations or choosing adjustment variables.

entries.title: Reason About Interventions and Counterfactuals
entries.description: Specify what changing an action would cause, distinguish observation from intervention, and assess causal effects, counterfactual comparisons, and identification assumptions.

entries.title: Design a Discriminating Test
entries.description: Choose the next diagnostic observation or small experiment by how clearly it separates plausible explanations, with explicit predicted outcomes and practical action branches.

entries.title: Define the Measurement
entries.description: Operationalize vague metrics such as success, speed, quality, reliability, and engagement with explicit units, events, collection rules, denominators, and error sources.

entries.title: Audit Sampling and Selection
entries.description: Audit selection bias in benchmarks, surveys, and reported success rates. Compare the target population with admitted, observed, completed, missing and excluded cases; retain crashes in the appropriate denominator.

entries.title: Update Beliefs with Base Rates and Evidence
entries.description: Use prior plausibility, likelihood ratios, base rates, and evidence dependence to revise explanations without confusing a reliable test with certainty or inventing probabilities.

entries.title: Propagate Uncertainty Through Calculations
entries.description: Carry uncertain inputs through formulas using intervals, sensitivity coefficients, covariance, or simulation; distinguish correlated error, standard uncertainty, and confidence bounds.

entries.title: Design an Informative Experiment
entries.description: Plan controlled comparisons, randomization, blocking, replication, factorial variation, and stopping rules so experiments answer the intended causal or performance question.

entries.title: Compare Effects and Practical Magnitude
entries.description: Estimate differences, ratios, paired effects, and uncertainty; separate practical importance from statistical significance and avoid interpreting an inconclusive result as equivalence.

entries.title: Expose Tradeoffs and Dominated Options
entries.description: Compare feasible alternatives across user objectives, remove dominated choices, and make cost, quality, speed, reliability, and flexibility tradeoffs explicit without arbitrary scoring.

entries.title: Test Sensitivity and Decision Thresholds
entries.description: Vary consequential assumptions, locate break-even points, and determine whether a conclusion survives plausible changes in cost, demand, timing, parameters, or model structure.

entries.title: Value Information Before Gathering It
entries.description: Choose whether to inspect, test, research, or act by estimating how new information could improve the decision relative to its cost, delay, and effect on available options.

entries.title: Sequence Decisions to Learn and Preserve Options
entries.description: Order actions by dependencies, information gained, reversibility, deadlines, and option value; start useful independent work while resolving uncertainties that affect expensive commitments.

entries.title: Prove Invariants Across State Changes
entries.description: Verify that a required property survives every allowed transition using initial conditions, inductive preservation, explicit assumptions, and counterexample traces.

entries.title: Find Minimal Counterexamples
entries.description: Challenge universal claims, algorithms, policies, and generalizations by constructing a small valid case that violates the stated property and reveals the missing condition.

entries.title: Validate Models Against Their Intended Use
entries.description: Check implementation, assumptions, predictive behavior, held-out cases, calibration, and deployment conditions separately so a fitted model or passing example is not mistaken for demonstrated usefulness.

entries.title: Map Structural Analogies and Transfer
entries.description: Transfer a useful method across domains by mapping relationships, identifying mismatches, testing a prediction, and extracting a narrow reusable rule with explicit conditions.

entries.title: State Machine Invariants
entries.description: Derive legal states, transitions and invariants for tasks, workflows and persistent processes. Use for cancellation races, resume bugs, impossible states, admission checks and lifecycle correctness.

entries.title: Trace Interface Contracts
entries.description: Find where a value changes meaning across APIs, adapters, serialization, storage and UI. Trace units, identity, optional fields, encoding, schemas and error semantics to the first broken boundary.

entries.title: Model Concurrent Interleavings
entries.description: Find race conditions by ordering reads, writes, waits and effects across workers. Use for lost updates, stale callbacks, duplicate execution, revision conflicts and cancellation interleavings.

entries.title: Recover Idempotent Effects
entries.description: Recover an API request after a timeout or interrupted response. Separate an uncertain committed effect from transport failure, reconcile the original intent, and prevent duplicate effects when deciding whether to retry.

entries.title: Reconcile Version Lineage
entries.description: Establish which changes are actually present in a source or installed artifact. Compare version labels, ancestry, patch content, build inputs and hashes for rollbacks, integration and release diagnosis.

entries.title: Localize Regressions
entries.description: Reduce a reproducible regression to the smallest supported change using stable predicates, good/bad boundaries and controlled comparisons. Use for bisecting performance, behavior and integration failures.

entries.title: Test Semantic Properties
entries.description: Derive tests from behavioral laws instead of copying implementation. Use invariants, round trips, metamorphic relations, boundary cases and shrinking to expose meaningful counterexamples.

entries.title: Calculate Memory Liveness
entries.description: Estimate actual peak memory from allocations and overlapping lifetimes. Use for RAM or VRAM requirements, model loading, temporary copies, fragmentation, cache growth and out-of-memory diagnosis.

entries.title: Profile Compute and Data Movement
entries.description: Identify whether execution is limited by arithmetic, memory traffic, transfers or scheduling. Use roofline bounds, measured bandwidth and focused profiling to choose effective performance changes.

entries.title: Analyze Execution Dependencies
entries.description: Analyze execution dependencies, overlap, queueing, startup and latency to locate the longest necessary path. Derive speedup bounds and distinguish usable completion from early screen display.

entries.title: Bound Queueing and Backpressure
entries.description: Diagnose growing queues, overload and retry amplification from arrival rates, service demand and deadlines. Derive stable capacity and backpressure behavior without assuming more concurrency always helps.

entries.title: Reason About Cache Validity
entries.description: Derive when cached results remain valid from semantic inputs and dependencies. Use for stale state, missing invalidation, incorrect cache keys, concurrent refresh and expensive recomputation.

entries.title: Analyze Computational Complexity and Scale
entries.description: Derive how time, memory and work grow with actual input dimensions. Use operation counts, empirical scaling, crossover analysis and worst-case structure to forecast computational feasibility.

entries.title: Benchmark Comparable Work
entries.description: Design fair performance comparisons with matched tasks, quality, artifacts, timing boundaries and hardware state. Separate cold start, warm throughput, latency, resource use and output correctness.

entries.title: Isolate Model and Runtime Failures
entries.description: Separate model limitations from conversion, precision, tokenizer, preprocessing and kernel defects. Use matched-runtime comparisons, layer traces and controlled ablations for inference diagnosis.

entries.title: Analyze Quantization Error
entries.description: Trace how clipping, rounding, grouping, calibration and accumulation affect model behavior. Use tensor-level error, activation sensitivity and selective precision experiments to diagnose quantized inference.

entries.title: Budget Context and KV Cache
entries.description: Calculate context memory from actual attention architecture, cache dtype and concurrency. Separate configured context length, allocated capacity, latency and demonstrated long-context accuracy.

entries.title: Diagnose Training Signals
entries.description: Trace examples, labels, losses, gradients and parameter updates to determine what training actually learns. Use for falling-loss failures, frozen parameters, masking defects and objective mismatch.

entries.title: Detect Evaluation Leakage
entries.description: Identify hidden information paths that inflate measured model performance. Inspect prediction-time availability, grouped duplicates, temporal splits, preprocessing fit and test-driven tuning.

entries.title: Test Distribution Transfer
entries.description: Assess whether learned behavior transfers when populations, sensors, timing, labels or mechanisms change. Diagnose distribution shift with subgroup tests, controlled comparisons and support checks.

entries.title: Inspect Multimodal Alignment
entries.description: Trace images, audio or video through preprocessing, patches, projectors, templates and output coordinates. Use for vision failures, missing media, token alignment and incorrect spatial interpretation.

entries.title: Model Conservation Networks
entries.description: Build balance equations for material, energy, charge or inventory across connected compartments. Use control volumes, accumulation and flow accounting to diagnose missing quantities and impossible models.

entries.title: Balance Thermal Power
entries.description: Derive temperature behavior from heat storage, power input and transport paths. Use thermal capacity, conductance, steady state and time constants to reason about cooling, heating and thermal limits.

entries.title: Reason About Forces and Constraints
entries.description: Derive mechanical behavior from a defined body, external forces and constraints. Use free-body models, equilibrium, acceleration, friction limits and moment balances to resolve motion problems.

entries.title: Select Physical Regimes
entries.description: Choose valid physical approximations and scaling rules from competing effects and dimensionless ratios. Use for prototype transfer, flow regimes, timescale separation and model applicability.

entries.title: Analyze Feedback Stability
entries.description: Analyze control feedback loops for stability, gain, delay and saturation. Derive closed-loop dynamics, identify when corrective action becomes unstable, and test the assumptions behind a stable operating range.

entries.title: Assess System Reliability
entries.description: Derive system failure from component dependencies, redundancy and common causes. Use series/parallel models, mission intervals and repair assumptions to assess reliability claims and failure exposure.

entries.title: Verify Simulation Convergence
entries.description: Separate solver convergence, discretization error, implementation correctness and physical validation. Use mesh/time refinement, conservation and independent reference cases to assess simulation evidence.

entries.title: Derive Unit Economics
entries.description: Derive contribution, break-even volume and scale limits from a business unit's revenue and incremental costs. Use for profitability, customer economics, service margins and cost-to-serve analysis.

entries.title: Reconcile Cash Timing
entries.description: Trace collections, payments, working capital and financing to explain how profitable activity can consume cash. Use for runway, liquidity, cash conversion and profit-to-cash reconciliation.

entries.title: Derive Pricing Response Thresholds
entries.description: Calculate how a price cut or increase changes contribution and required sales volume. Derive the break-even quantity with variable costs, demand response, customer mix and capacity steps made explicit.

entries.title: Map Market Substitution
entries.description: Identify competition through customer alternatives, switching costs and supply responses. Use for market boundaries, competitive analysis, substitutes, positioning and entry barriers.

entries.title: Compare Making, Buying and Contracting
entries.description: Compare internal development, procurement and partnership using lifecycle cost, adaptability, asset specificity and exit constraints. Use for build-versus-buy, outsourcing and vendor dependence.

entries.title: Reason About Commons and Externalities
entries.description: Trace shared-resource use, spillovers and institutional rules from benefits, costs and replenishment. Use for congestion, common resources, externalities, quotas and collective-action design.

entries.title: Derive Incentive Responses
entries.description: Map actions, observations and rewards to predict effort allocation and unintended behavior. Use for contracts, compensation, agent objectives, principal-agent problems and incentive compatibility.

entries.title: Test Metrics Against Adaptive Behavior
entries.description: Identify ways a target score can improve without the intended outcome. Use for KPI design, benchmark gaming, reward proxies, denominator shifts and measurement after incentives change.

entries.title: Locate Coordination Failures
entries.description: Trace information, authority, execution and feedback across handoffs. Use for decision rights, organizational bottlenecks, repeated escalation, unclear ownership and coordination failure.

entries.title: Explain Adoption Friction
entries.description: Identify the benefit, effort, uncertainty and complementary changes behind adoption behavior. Use for product adoption, organizational change, switching friction, onboarding and resistance to change.

entries.title: Construct Negotiation Trades
entries.description: Build concrete agreement packages from alternatives, constraints and different preferences across issues. Use for negotiation preparation, bargaining ranges, BATNA analysis and multi-issue trades.

entries.title: Identify Rules in Use
entries.description: Distinguish formal policy from actual allocation, enforcement, exceptions and revision practices. Use for institutional analysis, informal governance, rules in use and organizational behavior.

entries.title: Frame Intelligence Requirements
entries.description: Turn a broad research topic into decision-relevant questions and observable collection priorities. Use for intelligence requirements, collection plans, indicators, research scope and decision support.

entries.title: Compare Competing Accounts
entries.description: Compare plausible explanations against discriminating evidence without counting repeated claims or turning ordinal scores into probabilities. Use for competing hypotheses, contested narratives and alternative explanations.

entries.title: Test Adversarial Accounts
entries.description: Examine selective disclosure, concealment and fabrication using actor incentives and independently observable constraints. Use for deception analysis, strategic claims, manipulated evidence and adversarial narratives.

entries.title: Reconstruct Historical Causes
entries.description: Explain past events through chronology, contemporary information, mechanisms and bounded case comparison. Use for historical causation, archival evidence, hindsight bias and comparative historical analysis.

entries.title: Derive the User's Task Model
entries.description: Translate a feature request into the user's desired state change, required information and actions. Use for task analysis, user needs, product requirements, workflows and outcome-based design.

entries.title: Model Observable Interaction States
entries.description: Map user actions to visible states, feedback and recovery paths. Use for interface state machines, ambiguous submissions, error recovery, accessible feedback and end-to-end interaction design.

entries.title: Organize Information for Retrieval
entries.description: Build labels, categories and search routes from concrete retrieval tasks. Use for information architecture, navigation, taxonomies, skill discovery, terminology mismatch and findability.

entries.title: Derive Needs from Qualitative Evidence
entries.description: Separate observations, interpretations and proposed changes while comparing interviews and task sessions. Use for qualitative research, user interviews, thematic analysis, unmet needs and contradictory cases.

entries.title: Teach Through Conceptual Distinctions
entries.description: Teach a concept by helping a learner distinguish valid examples from near misses, explain the underlying rule, and transfer it to a new problem. Check understanding through a fresh application.

entries.title: Derive Policy Mechanisms and Delivery
entries.description: Expand an intervention into resources, delivery, behavior and outcomes, then test implementation dependencies. Use for theory of change, program evaluation, policy mechanisms and implementation feasibility.

entries.title: Trace Policy Incidence and Responses
entries.description: Trace how taxes, fees, subsidies or rules shift costs, prices, behavior and benefits across groups. Use for policy incidence, economic burden, distributional effects and behavioral response.

entries.title: Apply Legal Rules to Supported Facts
entries.description: Map current controlling authority to elements, exceptions and case facts. Use for legal analysis, jurisdiction, rule application, contract interpretation and distinguishing law from policy.
